scene-u01-pnew1-5.name: text#5
scene-u01-pnew1-5.text: Before clustering, ask: are the data clustered, random, or regular?

scene-u01-pnew1-6.name: text#6
scene-u01-pnew1-6.text: How to read: each panel holds $100$ points in the sampling window (unit square); the hypothesis is on top and the way to generate such reference data below.

scene-u01-pnew1-112.name: text#112
scene-u01-pnew1-112.text: Neyman–Scott: random centers in the window, Poisson counts per cluster, normal scatter around each center

scene-u01-pnew1-116.name: text#116
scene-u01-pnew1-116.text: Scattered uniformly at random in the window

scene-u01-pnew1-218.name: text#218
scene-u01-pnew1-218.text: Simply place points uniformly in the window

scene-u01-pnew1-324.name: text#324
scene-u01-pnew1-324.text: SSI: add points one by one; a new hypersphere may not intersect existing ones

scene-u01-pnew1-325.name: text#325
scene-u01-pnew1-325.text: Only clustered data are worth clustering; if randomness or regularity is accepted, forced clusters are meaningless

scene-u01-pnew2-5.name: text#5
scene-u01-pnew2-5.text: Boundary effect: in the same uniform data, a point near the edge has a different distance profile

scene-u01-pnew2-6.name: text#6
scene-u01-pnew2-6.text: How to read: the left shows $100$ uniform points, blue $\mathbf{x}$ near the center and orange $\mathbf{y}$ near the left edge; the right shows histograms of their distances to the other $99$ points.

scene-u01-pnew2-174.name: text#174
scene-u01-pnew2-174.text: An edge point has no neighbors outside, so its distances are longer; dashed lines are means

scene-u01-pnew2-176.name: text#176
scene-u01-pnew2-176.text: Estimating the window: a wrong window makes even uniform data look non-random

scene-u01-pnew2-177.name: text#177
scene-u01-pnew2-177.text: Convex hull: ties the test to this data set and is costly

scene-u01-pnew2-178.name: text#178
scene-u01-pnew2-178.text: Common substitute: a hypersphere at the mean holding half of the vectors

scene-u01-pnew2-179.name: text#179
scene-u01-pnew2-179.text: Easing the boundary effect: periodic extension or a smaller sampling frame

scene-u01-pnew2-181.name: text#181
scene-u01-pnew2-181.text: Redone data and distances computed by code [Added]

scene-u01-pnew3-5.name: text#5
scene-u01-pnew3-5.text: Each test watches one statistic: large or small points to clustering or regularity

scene-u01-pnew3-6.name: text#6
scene-u01-pnew3-6.text: How to read: each panel shows simulated means for three patterns (green clustered, gray random, purple regular); the dashed red line is the expectation under randomness.

scene-u01-pnew3-9.name: text#9
scene-u01-pnew3-9.text: One MST over $X$ and uniform points $X'$, $M=N=100$

scene-u01-pnew3-24.name: text#24
scene-u01-pnew3-24.text: $b$ compares probe-to-data with data-to-data nearest distances

scene-u01-pnew3-44.name: text#44
scene-u01-pnew3-44.text: strong against clustering, weak against regularity

scene-u01-pnew3-50.name: text#50
scene-u01-pnew3-50.text: source simulations: strong on regularity, limited on clustering

scene-u01-pnew3-59.name: text#59
scene-u01-pnew3-59.text: The blind spot of a left-tail test

scene-u01-pnew3-60.name: text#60
scene-u01-pnew3-60.text: Clustered data give mean $q'$ of $-9.74$, rejected in all $50$ runs; regular data give about $+4.2$, never rejected by the left tail. Not rejecting is not the same as random.

scene-u01-pnew3-64.name: text#64
scene-u01-pnew3-64.text: With the source definition ($\delta_j$ searched only in $X_1$) the means are $0.727$, $0.432$, $0.415$, hard to tell apart; the chart above uses the common variant.

steps.label: Three hypotheses
steps.speakerNotes: Random (H0: uniform in the window), regular (never too close, generated by SSI), clustered (generated by Neyman–Scott); only clustered data are worth clustering.

steps.label: Sampling window and boundary effect
steps.speakerNotes: In the same uniform data the center point has mean distance 0.38 and the edge point 0.66; estimate the window by the convex hull or a hypersphere holding half the vectors.

steps.label: Three tests
steps.speakerNotes: A small MST q points to clustering (31.4 vs. expected 100); a large Hopkins b points to clustering (common variant 0.98, 0.50, 0.23); a small Cox–Lewis R points to clustering.
